fields.statement: Verified at 1bf8725d. Read the diff: RetryStep(def, st, failed) keeps the sole-wait rule, then walks st.Steps back from the failed visit. It skips the failed step's own visits; retried entries are never in State.Steps. It follows command steps whose on.fail routes into the next step, and returns the sole wait whose on.pass is such a check, else failed. Traced the built-in ship-change: pr-green -> conflict-triage -> ci-triage gives wait-pr; rebased-green -> conflict-triage -> ci-triage gives wait-rebased. engine.go and api/run.go pass the state. Ran with RHIZA_* unset and GOTMPDIR/TMPDIR in a scratch dir. Inherited GOTMPDIR sits under ~/code/rhiza and breaks rhiza init in scripts. go test -trimpath ./internal/run/... ok. TestRetryStepAtWaitBeforeCheck covers: via a -> wait-a; via b (journal picks) -> wait-b; through a middle step -> wait-c; three triage visits -> wait-b; no predecessor, lone step, and previous not routing in -> the failed step. go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(run-resume-retry|run-ship-retry)' passed: run-resume-retry, run-resume-retry-wait, run-ship-retry-pending and the new run-ship-retry-ci-triage. That script uses a fake gh, red then green: dry-run says retried at step wait-pr, resume succeeds, wait-pr visit 2 (retried) passes, then pr-green passes. internal/api: 533 tests passed and none failed, including TestRunResumeRetry and the other Resume/Retry tests. The package overran 8-15 min timeouts on load-heavy tests unrelated to this diff (TestReadBudget 151s, TestLinkEndpointKinds 226s alone, which passed) at VM load 10-16. CI runs the full package. gofmt clean, go vet ./internal/run ok.
